notes.title: Jesus’ “brothers and sisters”
notes.intro: The Gospels mention Jesus’ brothers James, Joseph, Simon and Judas, and sisters. Traditions understand this differently.

views.label: Relatives or cousins
views.summary: Catholics hold that Mary remained a virgin; the Greek word for “brothers” can mean close relatives, as in the Old Testament.

views.label: Joseph’s children from a previous marriage
views.summary: Many Orthodox Christians, following early writers, understand them as Joseph’s children by an earlier wife, so Mary remained ever-virgin.
views.source: Protoevangelium of James (2nd century), followed by Orthodox tradition

views.label: Children of Mary and Joseph
views.summary: Many Protestants read them as Jesus’ younger half-siblings, born to Mary and Joseph after Jesus. (Luther, Calvin and Wesley themselves held Mary’s perpetual virginity.)
views.source: Common Protestant reading of Matthew 1:25 and 13:55–56
